blocks.content: 1. INTRODUCTION TO ECONOMIC SECTORS

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Primary Sector relies directly on natural resources and encompasses agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining.
The Secondary Sector transforms raw materials into finished goods through manufacturing, processing, and construction.
The Tertiary Sector provides support services like transport, banking, trade, and communication to enable other sectors.
Employment classification divides the economy into Organised (formal, secure, regulated) and Unorganised (informal, low security) sectors.
Ownership classification separates Public Sector entities (government-owned for welfare) from Private Sector enterprises (individually owned for profit).

blocks.content:
An economy consists of millions of economic activities. These activities are grouped into sectors

to understand how an economy functions, how people earn their livelihood and how development takes place.

An economic sector refers to a group of economic activities that are similar in nature.

The classification of economic activities helps in:

• Studying economic growth

• Understanding employment pattern

• Analysing contribution to GDP

• Framing government policies

• Understanding structural changes in the economy
2. NEED FOR CLASSIFICATION OF SECTORS

The classification of economic activities is necessary because:

1. It helps in measuring economic development

2. It helps in analysing employment generation

3. It helps in identifying backward sectors

4. It helps in planning economic policies

5. It helps in international comparison
3. PRIMARY SECTOR (AGRICULTURAL SECTOR)

The primary sector includes activities that involve direct extraction and use of natural resources.

It is the oldest sector of the economy and forms the base of all other sectors.
3.1 Activities under Primary Sector

• Agriculture

• Fishing

• Forestry

• Mining

• Animal husbandry

• Dairy farming

• Quarrying
3.2 Characteristics of Primary Sector

• Depends on natural factors like rainfall, soil and climate

• Seasonal in nature

• Low productivity

• Traditional methods of production

• Large labour force

• Low level of income

• Presence of disguised unemployment
3.3 Importance of Primary Sector

• Provides food to the entire population

• Supplies raw material to industries

• Main source of livelihood in India

• Supports industrial and service sectors

• Plays key role in rural development
3.4 Problems of Primary Sector

• Heavy dependence on monsoon

• Small and fragmented land holdings

• Lack of irrigation facilities

• Low mechanisation

• Poverty and low income

• Disguised unemployment

• Low access to credit
4. SECONDARY SECTOR (INDUSTRIAL SECTOR)

The secondary sector includes activities that involve processing of raw materials into finished goods.

It plays a crucial role in economic development and industrialisation.
4.1 Activities under Secondary Sector

• Manufacturing industries

• Construction

• Electricity generation

• Oil refining

• Cement and steel industries
4.2 Characteristics of Secondary Sector

• Uses machines and technology

• Capital intensive

• Higher productivity than primary sector

• Generates employment

• Encourages urbanisation
4.3 Importance of Secondary Sector

• Adds value to raw materials

• Increases national income

• Promotes industrial growth

• Increases exports

• Reduces dependence on agriculture
5. TERTIARY SECTOR (SERVICE SECTOR)

The tertiary sector provides services that help in the production and distribution of goods.

It does not produce goods but supports primary and secondary sectors.

rows: Extraction and utilization of natural resources

blocks.content: 5.1 Activities under Tertiary Sector

• Transport

• Banking

• Insurance

• Education

• Health services

• Tourism

• Trade

• Communication
5.2 Characteristics of Tertiary Sector

• Provides services

• Intangible output

• Fastest growing sector

• Highest contributor to GDP

• Knowledge and skill-based
5.3 Importance of Tertiary Sector

• Supports economic activities

• Creates employment

• Improves quality of life

• Promotes economic growth

• Backbone of modern economy
6. ORGANISED AND UNORGANISED SECTOR

Organised Sector:

• Registered with government

• Fixed working hours

• Job security

• Social security benefits

Unorganised Sector:

• Not registered

• No job security

• Low wages

• Poor working conditions
7. PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR

Public Sector:

• Owned and managed by government

• Welfare objective

• Examples: Railways, ONGC



Private Sector:

• Owned by individuals or companies

• Profit motive

• Examples: TCS, Reliance
8. SECTORAL SHIFT IN INDIA

items: The Tertiary Sector contributes the largest percentage to India's GDP, while the Primary Sector continues to employ the largest share of the workforce.
Disguised unemployment is a frequently tested concept primarily associated with the Indian agricultural sector.
Distinction between organised and unorganised sectors regarding social security benefits and working conditions is a core topic in competitive exams.

blocks.content:
India has experienced a shift from primary sector to tertiary sector.

Although agriculture employs the largest population, service sector contributes maximum to GDP.

Reasons:

• Industrialisation

• Urbanisation

• Education

• Growth of service sector
9. ROLE OF GOVERNMENT IN SECTORAL DEVELOPMENT

• Infrastructure development

• Skill development schemes

• Industrial policies

• Employment generation

• Support to MSMEs
10.  EXAM IMPORTANT POINTS

• Primary sector depends on nature

• Secondary sector adds value

• Tertiary sector provides services

• Service sector contributes maximum GDP

• Majority workers are in unorganised sector
11. CONCLUSION

The sectoral structure of the Indian economy reflects its level of development.

The shift from agriculture to services indicates economic progress.

Understanding economic sectors is essential for policy making and competitive examinations.
